questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "much".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **"So" **is a degree adverb. It is mostly used in situations where **"very"** is also a suitable word.
 
• The difference between **"so much" **and **"so many"** is similar to the **difference **between **much **and **many**. **"So much"** is used before** singular uncountable nouns**. **"So many"** is used before **plural nouns**__.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Nile is the ________ river of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, we are comparing** the Nile** river to all other rivers in the world.
 
• When making comparisons involving the highest degree, we use the** superlative** form of the** adjective**.
 
• The superlative form of the adjective** 'long**' is '**longest**'.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **'longest' **to indicate that the Nile is the river with the greatest length in the world.

Hence the correct sentence is ***The Nile is the longest river of the world*****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• While comparing two things, we use the comparative form of the adjective, such as 'longer'.
 
 
• **Example:** *The Nile is** longer **than the Amazon.*
 
 
 
• While comparing more than two objects or while indicating the highest degree, we use the **superlativ**e form of the adjective, such as '**longest**'.
 
 
• Example: *The Nile is the **longest** river in the world.*

questions.question:

__
 
• "'With' is the correct preposition used in this sentence because it indicates the relationship between the subject 'you' and the object 'us'. In this context, 'with' is used to show that the person being addressed is going to join the group of people who are already having breakfast. 
 
• 'With' is a preposition that is used to indicate association or accompaniment. It is used to show that two or more things or people are together or in the same place. In this sentence, 'with' is used to show that the person being addressed is going to be in the same place as the group of people who are already having breakfast. 
 
• In summary, 'with' is the correct preposition used in this sentence because it indicates the association and accompaniment of the person being addressed with the group of people who are already having breakfast."

Therefore, the correct sentence is:* Please sit down and have breakfast **with__** us.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank**

You've cleared the _________ examination, haven't you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'entrance'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word of the given fill in the blank is **'entrance'. **
 
• We know that the most appropriate phrase is **'Entrance examination'. **We know that **the entrance examination is cleared. **
 
• **Entrance exams** are the ones that we take to be accepted into a school, etc. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 

**Correct Answer:__** You've cleared the **entrance **examination, haven't you?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The given sentence is an example of **a question tag. **Some rules of the question tag as follows: 
 
• If the verb is in the past simple we use did. 
 
 
• *Example: They went to the cinema, didn't they?*
 
 
 
• When the statement contains a word with a negative meaning, the question tag needs to be positive. 
 
 
• *Example: They rarely eat in restaurants, do they?*
 
• In the above example 'rarely' is a negative word. Therefore, a positive question tag will be used.

questions.question:

The sentence talks about how a lot of tourists in India visit the valley of Kashmir, more often in the Spring and the Summer. 

__
 
• Given that the sentence is trying to **imply a specific period during which tourists prefer to visit the Valley of Kashmir**, we need an adverb that also implies this.

• 'Frequently' implies that the **'many tourists' visit the Valley of Kashmir more than once**, whereas it is very unlikely that tourists visit the same place more than once during the same trip. Thus, this option is incorrect.

• Understanding what **part of grammar fits into the given blank **will help the reader understand what can be kept or eliminated. 

Thus, the correct answer is **option 3. **

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blanks.

The Nile is the ________ river in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**longest**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The superlative form of the adjective "**long**" is "**longest**."
 
• The sentence compares the Nile River to all other rivers in the world, indicating that it is the longest among them.
 
• **Option 1** ("most long") is incorrect as it is not a valid construction in English grammar.
 
• **Option 2** ("long") is incorrect because it does not indicate a comparison.
 
• **Option 4** ("longer") is incorrect because it is used for comparative, not superlative, comparisons.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The Nile is the **longest**__ river in the world."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "most long"** is incorrect because "most" is not used with short adjectives like "long."
 
• **Option 2: "long"** is incorrect as it does not indicate a comparison or superlative degree.
 
• **Option 4: "longer"** is incorrect as it is used for comparing two entities, not for superlative comparisons.

__
 
• The use of **"many" **in this sentence emphasizes that there are numerous reasons for the trend of farms adopting automation.

• Using **"many"** suggests a variety of factors contributing to the trend, emphasizing the complexity and diversity of the reasons behind the shift towards automation in farming practices.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can fill the blank in the given sentence.

Out of all the flowers in the garden, the rose is the ____beautiful.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. most beautiful .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When comparing more than two items or people, we use the superlative form of the adjective.
 
• The superlative form of "beautiful" is "most beautiful".
 
• Superlatives are often preceded by "the" when used in sentences.

Correct sentence: *Out of all the flowers in the garden, the rose is the **most beautiful**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Form:**

 
 
• **Usage:** Used to compare two items or people.
 
• **Structure:** Adjective + "er" or "more" + adjective.
 
• **Example:** She is more beautiful than her sister.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Form:**
 
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare more than two items or people, indicating the highest degree of the quality.
 
• **Structure:** Adjective + "est" or "most" + adjective.
 
• **Example:** She is the most beautiful girl in the class.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

The flat ________ is nice but the approach road is too narrow and congested.
questions.solution:
Here, one should have a basic understanding of pronouns to find the correct answer.

In the subject, the flat [non-living] is being talked about so the reflexive pronoun will be itself.

**Oneself**: it is the reflexive form of the pronoun 'one' when it refers to people in general or to the person speaking.

*Ex: One has to learn to control oneself.*

**Herself**: it is used to refer to a female object of a verb, that is the same person or animal as the subject of the verb.

*Ex: She kept telling herself that nothing was wrong.*

**Himself**: it is used to refer to a male object of a verb that is the same person or animal as the subject of the verb.

*Ex: He'd cut himself while shaving.*

**Itself**: it is used when the subject of the verb is "it" and the object is the same thing, animal, situation, or idea.

*Ex: The cat licked itself all over.*

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Prem Chand, _______ mainly wrote about rural India, was a great Hindi writer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'who'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **That **is used in defining clauses.

 
 
• **That **का प्रयोग defining clauses में किया जाता है।​

 
 
• **Example**: *My bike **that **has a broken seat is in the garage.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Whom*** *is simply the objective case of **who**, which means that it's the form of **who** that is in the object position in a sentence.
 
 
• **Whom **केवल **who **का objective मामला है, जिसका अर्थ है कि यह वह रूप है जो एक वाक्य में object की स्थिति में है।​
 
 
• **Example**: *He saw the faces of those whom he loved at his birthday celebration. *
 
 
 
 
 
• **Who **is a pronoun, which means that it's used instead of a noun or noun phrase to refer to a noun/noun phrase that has already been mentioned or that does not need to be named specifically.
 
 
• एक सर्वनाम who है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसका उपयोग संज्ञा या संज्ञा वाक्यांश के बजाय एक संज्ञा / संज्ञा वाक्यांश को संदर्भित करने के लिए किया जाता है जिसका पहले ही उल्लेख किया जा चुका है या जिसे विशेष रूप से नाम देने की आवश्यकता नहीं है।​
 
 
• **Example**: ***Who** is your father?*
 
 
 
 
 
• ***​*Which** introduces non-defining clauses.
 
 
• **Which** का प्रयोग non- defining clauses में किया जाता है।​
 
 
• **Example**: *She seemed more talkative than usual, **which** was because she was nervous.*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​*Correct sentence__:* **Prem Chand, **who **mainly wrote about rural India, was a great Hindi writer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Subject pronouns are pronouns that replace the subject in the sentence. 
 
• The subject pronouns are we, you, he, she, it, and they.
 
• Object pronouns do not replace the subject.
 
• Instead, an object pronoun would replace the object in the sentence.
 
• The object is the part of the sentence that is being done to, from or with the action.
 
• The object pronouns are me, you, him, her, it, us, and them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**informative**" is an adjective that describes something that provides useful or interesting information.
 
• The adverb "**very**" is used to modify adjectives in their base form, not their comparative or superlative forms.
 
• Options like "**more informative**" and "**most informative**" are incorrect here because they are not preceded by appropriate comparative structures (e.g., "than" or a list for comparison).
 
• "**Information**" is a noun, and using it directly after "very" would be grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The discussion led by the scientist was very **informative**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Use "**informative**" when describing events, lectures, or discussions that provide knowledge or insight.
 
• Example: "The documentary was highly informative and well-researched."
 
• The word "**very**" intensifies the adjective, and must be followed by an adjective in the correct degree.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I think I have left ______ lunchbox at your house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **my**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the use of the given options.
 
 
• **I**: We use the pronoun "**I**" when the person speaking is doing the action, either alone or with someone else.
 
• **My**: It shows possession or ownership of the noun. It describes something that belongs to the speaker.
 
• **Me**: We use the pronoun "**me**" when the person speaking is receiving the action of the verb in some way, either directly or indirectly.
 
• **Mine**: It can refer to a singular or plural noun, and it can be used as the subject, object, or complement of a verb or the object of a preposition.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is also the speaker and he/she is talking about the **ownership of the lunchbox**.
 
• Therefore, according to the usage of the pronouns "**my**" should be used here.
 
• Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I am not going to buy ______ toys for you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**these**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate determiner for the given blank is '**these**'.
 
• '**This**' and '**these**' are used to point to something near you. For a singular thing, use **this**. For a plural thing, use **these**. 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *I like **this** phone a lot.*
 
• *Do you like **these** shoes?*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence '**toys**' is **plural** hence '**these**' should be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I am not going to buy **these** toys for you.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

The vibrations from wind instruments ______ always positive and good ______ your breathing and health.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. are; for. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• According to the **Subject-Verb Agreement rule**, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
• **‘The vibrations****’ is a plural subject.** So the verb that accompanies it must be plural too. This helps to cancel out options 1 and 3.
 
• Now option 4 is left. 'Were' is a plural verb but 'to' is the incorrect preposition here. Some instances where 'to' is used are given below:
 
 
• Destination- I’m going to Europe.
 
• Distance- It’s about five miles from my house to the church.
 
• Comparing- I prefer sleeping to exercising.
 
• Giving- He gave the apple to his sister.
 
• Motive- He came here to see you.
 
 
 
• Meanwhile, **‘for’ here is used while stating the benefit of something.** An example of using ‘for’ for this is: *Vitamin C is good for your health. *
 
• Hence we have to use **‘are’(plural verb)** in the first blank and **‘for’(correct preposition)** in the second blank.

**The correct sentence is: ***The vibrations from wind instruments **are** always positive and good **for **your breathing and health.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The detail given by the instructor was the ______ one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**most updated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "most updated" refers to the version that is the latest or most current. (अधिकतम अद्यतन)
 
• In the context, "the most updated" suggests that the detail provided is the most recent and relevant.
 
• The other options: "more updation," "updating," and "updates" do not convey the intended meaning of being the latest or most recent version in this context.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The detail given by the instructor was the most updated__ one.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **More updation (अधिक अद्यतन)**: is grammatically incorrect in this context. "Updation" is a less commonly used term and "more" does not fit appropriately with it.
 
• **Updating (अद्यतन करना)**: refers to the process of making something more current, but it does not fit the context of describing the most current version.
 
• **Updates (अद्यतन)**: refers to multiple new pieces of information or changes, but it does not convey the meaning of being the most recent or most up-to-date version.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

She had won the match by the time we ______ the venue.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 'reached'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Rule**__: If** two actions take place in the past**, one after the other, the **first action** will be in the** Past Perfect **Tense and the **second action** will be in the **Simple Past** Tense.
 
• In the given sentence, the** first action** is in the **past perfect** tense. 
 
• The structure of the past perfect tense is** 'Subject + had + V3 + object'. **
 
• So, the **second action **should be in the **Simple Past **Tense i.e. **'subject + V2 + object'**.

 

Therefore, **option 2** 'reached' which is in **V₂ form** is the correct answer.
